items.title: Oil Climbs on Threats of a Widening War in Middle East
items.snippet: Brent oil traded at the highest level since May on Friday. Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed recent attacks on the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu, as well as deadly strikes on an oil field and airport in the kingdom. The flareup threatens to widen hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz, where crude exports have recovered to near prewar levels. Abeer Abu Omar reports on Bloomberg Television. -----

Failte-Sigenergy JV to Invest in India with Inverter, Battery Storage Plants
items.snippet: Chinese energy storage firm Sigenergy forms a JV with Failte Energy of India to invest $250 mn in India, With this investment, JV will set up production facilities for inverter and battery energy storage systems. Sigenergy plans to launch its inverter plant by the second quarter of 2027.

items.title: Swiggy to Transition Instamart to Inventory Model Within Three Quarters
items.snippet: Swiggy wants to move Instamart to an inventory-led strategy in the next three quarters, which could enhance working capital by 8-10 days and increase contribution margins by 80 basis points. The move will offer Instamart more say over price, product selection and availability.

items.title: Vikram Solar Set to Launch Cell Production at 9 GW Tamil Nadu Facility in 2026
items.snippet: Vikram Solar will commission production at its 9 GW N-type TOPCon solar cell plant in Gangaikondan, Tamil Nadu, in December 2026. The factory is expected to be commissioned in phases and is intended to lessen India’s reliance on imported solar cells.

items.title: OpenAI Reduces Valuation Target to $1.25 Trillion Amid $150 Billion Cut
items.snippet: OpenAI is apparently planning to raise about $30 billion from investors and has dropped its valuation aim by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion. The increased valuation comes as the growing scrutiny over AI spending, infrastructure expenses and long-term profitability.

items.title: Barclays to Slash 5,000 Jobs in AI Push Despite 12% Rise in Q3 Profit
items.snippet: Barclays is planning to shed 5,000 positions, or 5% of its staff, in an AI-driven cost-cutting move. The UK bank wants to use technology and automation to save fixed expenses and over 60 per cent of the employment being cut are support activities.
